question: After matching the retained P4BS second-order spectrum, do real uniform-film scan residuals support finite-capacity bounded cloud occupancy over an unbounded Gaussian Thomas field in candidate-independent higher-order statistics?

fixed_models.gaussian_control: P4BU finite-support Thomas field with unbounded normal innovations
fixed_models.bounded_candidate: P4CA finite-support Thomas field with 16-trial p=0.5 occupancy innovations

observed_roles.development: all eight P4R colour uniform scans, each scan aggregated across the original four fixed crops and RGB channels
observed_roles.confirmation: all three P4Z1 B&W uniform scans, each scan aggregated across the original nine fixed crops

preprocessing.residual: quadratic detrend of code divided by crop mean
preprocessing.normalization: subtract residual mean and divide by population RMS

higher_order_metrics.excursion_feature: log1p connected-component count per megapixel, separately for positive and negative excursions
higher_order_metrics.scan_winner: bounded candidate must have lower RMSE in at least two of marginal quantiles, local-RMS quantiles and excursion topology

branch_rule.pass: Retain bounded occupancy only as a generic same-scanner effective higher-order innovation mechanism and open one independently frozen density-domain synthetic integration audit.
branch_rule.fail: Close the exact P4CA higher-order mechanism without changing occupancy, features, crops, aggregation or gates; retain P4BS second-order evidence and seek a new observation or mechanism.

forbidden: fit either model, feature, crop, threshold or gate to observed higher-order statistics
treat scanner-convolved residual topology as microscopic grain or dye-cloud truth
use stock labels or photograph content
clip, winsorize, normalize realized variance or alter field tails
promote a renderer, stock profile or product default
claim_ceiling: Candidate-independent higher-order mechanism comparison on existing same-scanner uniform scans; not microscopic, stock, process, density, scanner-independent, calibrated or product evidence.
